s: Because of the Bland-Allison Act, the U.S. Mint struck large quantities of the Morgan Dollar from 1878 to 1904 in Carson City, San Francisco, New Orleans, and Denver (many Morgan Dollars have a mint mark indicating in which city they were produced). The Act required the Treasury to buy between two and four million dollars in silver each month to be struck into one dollar coins.
